newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Pilmico eyes rising meat consumption.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Pilmico eyes rising meat consumption.

text.p: The Philippines' Pilmico Foods Corp said on Monday it hopes to cash in on rising domestic meat consumption.
"We expect per capita meat consumption in the Philippines to continue to rise from the present 12 to 14 kilos per year due to rising disposable income," president Antonio Moraza said.
Pilmico, a unit of Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc, signed a joint venture with U.S.-based firms Tyson Foods Inc and PM Nutrition Company Inc.
The joint venture plans to establish feed mill with a capacity of 120,000 tonnes a year and swine farms in central Luzon for the domestic market at a projected cost of about $25 million.
"We hope to be in operation by the third quarter," Moraza told a news conference after the signing ceremony.
Pilmico is investing an initial $6.5 million for its 50 percent stake in the joint venture, while the two U.S. firms will invest $3.25 million each.
Moraza said his group has approached various financial institutions, including the International Finance Corp to finance the remaining cost of the project.
He said there is still room for a new feed miller and swine producer in the domestic market which can offer a "more affordable price."
Tyson Foods is a large poultry processor, while PM Nutrition Company is a wholly-owned unit of Purina Mills Inc, a big producer of commercial animal feeds in the United States.

Pilmico is one of the country's largest flour millers. The expansion of its mill in Iligan city in southern Philippines from 600 to 1,150 tonnes is expected to be completed next month, said Aboitiz chief operating officer Erramon Aboitiz.
